lead: A start is run by flags; the sounds only draw your eye to them. Learn the sequence, what each preparatory flag threatens, and what to do when you are over the line.

qa.q: How does the five-minute starting sequence work under rule 26?
qa.a: Under **rule 26** the class flag goes up at 5 minutes, the preparatory flag at 4 and down at 1, and the class flag comes down at the start. Times are taken from the flags, not the sounds.

head: To go
Flag

Signal
rows: P, I, Z, Z with I, U or black up

blocks.p: **Times are taken from the flags**: a missing horn changes nothing, and a horn without the flag is no signal. The sailing instructions may change the five minutes. The next class's warning comes with or after the start before it. You are **racing** from your preparatory signal.

sections.title: What the last minute can cost

qa.q: What happens if I'm in the triangle in the last minute under the black flag, rule 30.4?
qa.a: You are disqualified without a hearing: under the **black flag**, a boat identified in the triangle between the ends of the line and the first mark in the last minute is scored BFD and cannot sail a restart.

blocks.p: Flag **P** adds nothing. The others police the **last minute** before your starting signal. Under **I**, a boat with any part of her hull on the course side must sail round an end, across an extension of the line, to the pre-start side before starting. **Z**, **U** and **black** concern the triangle between the ends of the line and the first mark: a boat identified there is penalised without a hearing, even if she is behind the line at the gun.

fig.note: Z, U, black: stay out of the triangle in the last minute

head: Flag
Penalty
After a recall or resail
rows: Stands: number displayed, no restart for you

blocks.p: None applies if the race is postponed or abandoned before the starting signal. The 20 % is of the score for not finishing, entries plus one, rounded to a tenth of a point: fifth of 30 becomes 5 + 6.2 = 11.2. Sail a restart after your number was displayed and that disqualification cannot be discarded. Z with I: both rules apply.

sections.title: Hull behind the line at the gun

qa.q: I was over the line at the starting signal: what must I do to start properly?
qa.a: Return your whole hull to the pre-start side of the line or its extensions, keeping clear of boats that are not returning, and cross again. Until then you have not **started**; sail on and you are scored OCS.

refs: RRS definition Start, RRS 28.1, Basic Principle Sportsmanship

blocks.p: You **start** when your hull, having been entirely on the pre-start side at or after your starting signal, crosses the line from that side. Only the hull counts, not a bowsprit or crew. Over at the signal, you have not started, whatever the cause and whether or not anyone tells you.

fig.note: Over at the gun: back below the line, then start

blocks.p: Bring the whole hull back to the pre-start side of the line or its extensions, by any route under flag P, round an end under flag I, and cross again. While returning after your starting signal you keep clear of boats that are not, until your hull is completely on the pre-start side; then your ordinary rights are back. Sail on and you are scored OCS.

sections.title: X for some, First Substitute for all

qa.q: What is the difference between flag X and First Substitute at a race start?
qa.a: Flag X with one sound is an **individual recall**: boats over the line return and start. First Substitute with two sounds is a general recall: racing stops, and the new warning comes one minute after it is lowered.

blocks.p: **Individual recall**: flag X with one sound, promptly after the start, when a boat is over or must round an end. The committee need not hail numbers. X stays up until those boats have returned, but no later than four minutes after the start or one minute before the next start.

**General recall**: First Substitute with two sounds, when the committee cannot identify the boats over or erred in the procedure. Racing stops. The new warning comes one minute after First Substitute is lowered. A breach in the recalled start is not penalised, except under rules 2, 30.2, 30.4 and 69, or rule 14 with injury or serious damage.

sections.title: AP before the start, N after it

qa.q: What does the AP flag mean in a sailing race, and when is the next start?
qa.a: **AP** with two sounds postpones races not yet started; the warning signal comes one minute after AP is lowered. Over a numeral pennant 1–9 it postpones by that many hours; over A, no more racing today.

refs: RRS race signals (AP over numeral pennant)
RRS 26, race signals (AP over numeral pennant)

head: Signal
Sounds
Meaning
rows: Races not started are postponed; warning 1 minute after AP comes down
Postponed 1–9 hours from the scheduled start
Races that have started are abandoned: return to the starting area

blocks.p: Before the starting signal the committee may postpone or abandon for any reason. It may change the course until the warning signal and move a starting mark until the preparatory signal. **L** afloat: come within hail or follow this vessel. **Y**: wear personal flotation devices.

sections.title: Right of way on the line

qa.q: Do I get mark-room at the committee boat when starting a race?
qa.a: No: a **starting mark** surrounded by navigable water gives no mark-room as boats approach it to start, so a windward boat has no claim on the gap. The usual rules apply: port keeps clear of starboard, windward of leeward.

fig.note: A reaches in to windward: no room at the committee boat

blocks.p: Before the gun the usual rules decide: port keeps clear of starboard, windward of leeward. **A starting mark surrounded by navigable water gives no mark-room** as boats approach it to start, so a boat reaching in to windward has no claim on the gap at the committee boat. The leeward boat may hold her course or luff, giving room to keep clear when she changes course.

Before the starting signal there is no proper course, so rule 17 does not stop a luff. Touch a starting mark while racing: one-turn penalty, unless another boat's breach forced you onto it. A boat backing a sail to move astern keeps clear.

qa.q: What do OCS, ZFP, UFD and BFD mean on race results?
qa.a: **OCS**: over the line at the starting signal and did not start; ZFP: 20 % penalty under flag Z; UFD and BFD: disqualified under flag U or the black flag. All are scored without a hearing; if wrong, request redress.

head: Score
Meaning
rows: Over at the starting signal and did not start, or broke rule 30.1: entries plus one
Disqualified under flag U · under the black flag
Did not start, e.g. past the time limit in the sailing instructions

blocks.p: The committee gives these scores **without a hearing**. If it erred, request **redress** in time: the remedy for an improper action or omission of the committee that made your score significantly worse, such as a wrong OCS. Current or a dying breeze is no ground.
